To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nucleotide sequence of the genome of HaSV has been determined and the genes expressed in bacteria.
the sequence of RNA2, a member of the tetravirus family, was determined and the coat and non-structural proteins were expressed in bacteria.
the nucleotide sequence of the RNA of the insect virus HaSV was determined and the gene products were expressed in bacteria and the coat protein produced virus-like particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of RNA2 of HaSV and its expression in bacteria.

the development of an efficient system for the production of recombinant virus-like particles in bacteria and with the identification of a new type of tRNA-like structure in the 3' non-coding region of a tetravirus genome.
the molecular biology of tetraviruses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HaSV capsid is composed of two proteins, the major 71 kDa protein (p71) and a 17 kD protein (p17), and that p17 is a major component of the capsid.
HaSV RNA2 has two overlapping ORFs encoding a PEST protein and a coat protein precursor which is cleaved into the coat proteins.
the sequence of RNA2 and the properties of the expressed proteins of HaSV are very similar to those of Nudaurelia Omega virus and that they are members of the same virus genus, the Nudaurenivirus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have characterized the complete sequence of RNA2 and its gene products, determined that the coat protein precursor is 66% homologous to Nodavirus, that p71 does not form virus-like particles in Escherichia coli, but p17 produces hollow tube-like structures and that both proteins are likely to be produced by a leaky scanning mechanism in the host cell.

the HaSV genome is similar in structure to other tetraviruses and the coat protein gene is highly conserved between tetraviruses, but the coat protein is highly divergent and the virus particles are not serologically cross-reactive.

the HaSV genome is similar in structure and organization to that of Nudaurelia beta virus (NbV) and that the coat protein precursor is similar in amino acid sequence to that of NbV but not in structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complete genome sequence of HaSV has been determined and that the coat protein gene is expressed in bacteria.
we were able to show that tetravirus capsids are assembled from a 7 kDa protein and a 64 kDa protein and not from a 71 kDa protein as previously thought.
the complete sequence of the RNA2 of HaSV has been determined and the genes of RNA2 have been expressed in bacteria.
